open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” in `models`, but `canonical_values` also “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Which module owns the disclosure-class order: `models`, or `canonical_values`?
options: `models` owns the enumeration and its order; `canonical_values` only applies that order
`canonical_values` owns the order as well as the highest-class operation
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the order, and `canonical_values` owns only comparison and highest-class computation.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile M22 creation
open_points.text: “Two have several, on purpose: StoredValue M21 ... and NodeExecution M23” conflicts with “The module that writes a StoredValue M21 or a SpooledFile M22 sets its class” and assigns SpooledFile production to both `runs` and `effects`.
open_points.question: Who owns creation of a SpooledFile record: `store` alone, or both `runs` and `effects` according to the producing node kind?
options: `store` creates every SpooledFile from facts supplied by `runs` or `effects`
`runs` and `effects` are co-writers of SpooledFile records through `store`
One higher module owns all SpooledFile records
open_points.default_guess: `store` owns atomic SpooledFile creation and persistence, while `runs` or `effects` supplies the class and producing-attempt facts.

open_points.subject: randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: “`trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel” names no State 3 module that owns random identifier generation or collision retry.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation and the retry when a generated identifier already exists?
options: Each domain module mints IDs for the records it owns
`store` mints all entity IDs while inserting records
A shared lower-level module owns random-ID generation
open_points.default_guess: `store` mints and collision-checks the identifier in the transaction that inserts the record.

open_points.subject: actor of automatic kernel work
open_points.text: State 0 says the kernel’s records “name it as the actor, so no automatic step looks like a human decision,” while M27 says records including `AdmissionVerdict`, `TrialExecution`, `NodeExecution` and `EffectAttempt` “name no actor: it is the kernel's work.”
open_points.question: Must every record produced by an automatic kernel step explicitly carry `Actor(kind=kernel)`, or is absence of an actor the representation of kernel work for the listed record types?
options: Every automatic record explicitly names the kernel actor
The listed record types omit an actor and kernel authorship is inferred from record type or parent
Only automatic decisions and activations name the kernel; observations omit actors
open_points.default_guess: Only records with an actor/by field explicitly name the kernel; observation records omit an actor, and the State 0 wording is narrowed accordingly.
